text: Bennett students hunt through long policy PDFs and notices for rules on attendance, exams, fees and hostel, and seniors give different answers.
CampusSage answers only from the official policy documents and quotes the exact clause and section, or says the policy does not cover it.
Old prompt V1 (our Milestone 1 baseline): one user message, four rules, no status field, only High/Low confidence.
Improved prompt V3: exact quotes, section from the excerpt header, rules for contradictions, injection and Hinglish, a confidence rubric, a self-check and 2 examples.
Same question, same retrieved clauses for every version: only the prompt changes. The Evaluation page measures each version on the full test set.
Real Claude output for test T10. Old prompt V1 decides by itself which late fee applies and has no Status field, so the app must guess it.
Improved prompt V3, same question and excerpts: Claude reports Conflicting Evidence and quotes both clauses, each verified word for word.
All 14 tests on Claude: pass rate V1 64% → V2 93% → V3 100%; citation accuracy 50% → 100%; hallucination 29% → 0%.
Test T01: a normal attendance question. The answer quotes Attendance Policy Section 2.1, verified word for word against the document.
Test T10: two documents disagree on the late fee. CampusSage reports Conflicting Evidence and quotes both clauses instead of picking one.
Test T06: a vague question gets one clarifying question. The reply "fee payment" is then answered from Fee Regulations Section 1.2.
Test T08: the policies do not cover exchange programmes, so CampusSage says so and names the office to contact instead of guessing.
Policy library: a new PDF is uploaded, split into numbered clauses and indexed in seconds, ready to be cited.
Done: full RAG web app, prompts V1 to V3 compared on Claude (V3 passes 14/14), and 22 tests in demo mode (21 pass; holdout H05 fails).
Next for Milestone 3: repeat the Claude runs to measure consistency, add Hinglish query rewriting, and load Bennett public documents with OCR.
